auxiliary_material: The text details mechanisms by which specific microbes (e.g., Fusobacterium nucleatum, Akkermansia muciniphila) modulate ICI efficacy in preclinical models and early clinical settings, providing context for why Phase 3 trials are needed. It mentions ongoing trials (NCT04729322, NCT04130763) but does not specify their phase as III or provide estimated completion times for key Phase 3 studies like CanBiome2.

remaining_gap: The material does not identify specific ongoing key Phase 3 trials (e.g., CanBiome2) by name, sponsor, or estimated completion time, leaving the second success criterion unaddressed. It confirms the lack of completed Phase 3 data but does not provide the forward-looking trial registry details required to fully map the Phase 3 landscape. The success criterion of confirming published Phase 3 primary endpoints (OS/PFS) is explicitly negative based on this text, but the criterion to identify ongoing Phase 3 timelines remains open.
useful_material: This study surveyed 29 clinical trials of microbiome modulators in colorectal cancer (CRC) as of June 30, 2025, finding that the pipeline is predominantly early-phase (Phase I, I/II, and II), with no mention of completed Phase 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) publishing primary endpoints like overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS). It reports efficacy data from Phase II trials (e.g., RENMIN-215 trial showing 20% ORR and 9.6 months mPFS with FMT plus ICIs in MSS CRC) and meta-analyses of early-phase trials, explicitly stating that 'the clinical pipeline for MMs in CRC remains predominantly early-phase'. This confirms the absence of completed large-scale Phase 3 evidence in the surveyed literature.
